effect_estimate.comment: Descriptive quantitative findings from the cross-sectional household survey; Tables 1-3 and Figures 1-3 are embedded images not rendered as text in the source extract, so all reported figures are taken strictly from the printed text and notes. No inferential regression or p-values are reported.
effect_estimate.value: In the rural community of Cristais (n = 232 surveyed households), excluded from a formal piped Water Supply System (WSS) and denied legal right to draw water from the adjacent Integration Canal (prioritized by Ceará state water policy for metropolitan Fortaleza and industrial complexes despite Act Nº 9.433/1997 prioritizing human consumption), substantial intra-community inequalities in water access were documented: (1) Quantity (n = 193 measurable households): 28.5% (55/193) consumed <20 L/inhabitant/day, 40.9% (79/193) consumed 20-50 L/inhabitant/day, and only 30.6% exceeded 50 L/inhabitant/day; (2) Physical accessibility: 35.8% of households traveled outside immediate surroundings to collect water, of whom 53.0% spent 5-30 minutes per trip and 37.3% spent >30 minutes per trip; (3) Affordability and informal fees: while 40.5% spent nothing on water and 19.0% spent up to 3% of household income, roughly 40% spent >3% of income (with households earning <=1 minimum salary polarized between 0% and >5% of income, whereas 52% of households earning >2 minimum salaries spent <=3%), driven by informal water carters charging ~R$ 4.00 (US$ 1.76) per 200 L, or R$ 20.00/m³ (US$ 8.82/m³)—nearly 10 times CAGECE's regular residential tariff of R$ 2.15/m³ (US$ 0.95/m³) and 25 times CAGECE's social tariff of R$ 0.79/m³ (US$ 0.35/m³).
effect_estimate.where_found: PDF pp. 9-10, Section 2.2; PDF pp. 11-15, Section 3; PDF pp. 15-16, Section 4; PDF pp. 16-17, Notes ii & viii

mechanism_certainty.comment: Capped at 2 by the cross-sectional design ceiling (JBI tool). Assigned 2 because the study directly observes and empirically documents in Cristais both the institutional/service-area exclusion from the adjacent Integration Canal and formal WSS coverage and the informal transport fee/appropriation mechanism operating on household water quantity, collection time, and income expenditure.
mechanism_certainty.where_found: PDF pp. 9-10, Section 2.2; PDF pp. 11-15, Section 3; PDF pp. 15-16, Section 4

mechanism_flags.comment: State water allocation planning and urban/industrial bias exclude rural Cristais from formal WSS service areas and legal access to the adjacent Integration Canal despite statutory human-consumption priority under Act Nº 9.433/1997 (ELIGIBILITY: planning, service_area), forcing reliance on self-fetching or informal water deliverers charging R$ 20.00/m³—25 times the regulated CAGECE social tariff—while appropriating public cistern supplies (BURDEN: fees).
